transcript:
User: Hey! So I'm Sofia — I run a real estate office here in Houston. Your ad was talking about missed calls? That's literally me.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Sofia — makes total sense, real estate phones are nonstop. When you say “that’s literally me,” what’s actually happening with those missed calls in your office right now?
User: I don't track it exactly, but maybe 25 or 30 calls a week slip through. It's chaotic!
Agent: Got it, 25–30 a week is a lot of people not getting through — that’s definitely real money in real estate. When those calls slip through, who’s supposed to be answering — do you have a front desk, or is it you and the agents juggling the phones?
User: It's me and the agents juggling. No front desk. It's a circus! Tell me more about your service.
Agent: Yeah, I can picture that — phones ringing while you’re trying to write offers and show houses. So, in a sentence: we make sure when you and your agents can’t grab the phone, those calls still get answered live, qualified, and turned into appointments or messages so you’re not losing deals when it’s “a circus.”  

So I don’t over-explain, what matters most to you right now — catching new buyer/seller leads, or making sure existing clients aren’t getting frustrated when no one picks up?
User: Honestly, both! New leads are crucial, but keeping current clients happy is non-negotiable. How soon can we start?
Agent: Yeah, that totally tracks for a real estate office — you can’t afford to drop either side.  

So when one of those 25–30 a week hits voicemail instead of a live person, what do you notice happens — do they usually leave a message, or do they just call the next agent down the street?
User: Most don't leave messages. They probably move on to the next agent. It's a nightmare!
Agent: Yeah, that’s exactly what I hear from a lot of brokers — that “next agent” is basically your competition on speed dial.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through what that nightmare is costing you in real dollars each month, or has it just been a gut feeling so far?
User: It's mostly been a gut feeling, but I'm sure it's costing me a lot. I'd love to know more!
Agent: Makes sense, most owners feel it long before they ever see it on paper.  

Mind if we do a super quick calculation together on what those missed calls are likely costing you every month — just ballpark, using your numbers?
User: Sure, let's do it. I could use a wake-up call on what I'm losing every month!
Agent: Love that, Sofia — let’s make it real, then.  

So ballpark, out of those calls that slip through — how many a week would you say actually hit voicemail or just ring out: closer to 25 or 30?
User: I mean, probably closer to 25. But hey, let's focus on fixing it!
Agent: Got it, let’s use 25.  

Out of those 25 missed each week, what percentage do you think would’ve turned into real clients if someone had picked up — maybe half, around 50%, or would you say less?
User: I'd say around 50% could've turned into clients. I really need to fix this!
Agent: Mhm, that’s a big chunk.  

And in your world, when one of those turns into a client, what’s a reasonable average commission or fee per closed deal — are we talking more like $3,000, $5,000, or higher?
User: Oh, definitely higher! I'd say on average, each closed deal brings in about $8,000.
Agent: Perfect, let’s use $8,000 then.  

So just using *your* numbers, if you’d caught even 50% of those 25 missed calls, that’s about $100,000 a week in closed deals you’re not even getting a shot at… and over a month, that’s roughly $433,000 — how does that land hearing it that way?
User: Wow, hearing that number is shocking. I really need this service to stop losing that much potential revenue!
Agent: Yeah, it’s a serious wake-up call when you see it in black and white.  

So… to actually stop that leak and show you exactly how this would work for your office, would you be open to a quick 20‑minute walkthrough this week to see your numbers and the setup — is later today or tomorrow better for you?
User: Oh, next week is packed, but wait — actually, tomorrow works! Which slots do you have available?
Agent: Got it, tomorrow is great.  

Before we look at times, quick thing — is the number you’re calling from the best number to text a confirmation to, or do you prefer a different one?
User: Yes, this number works perfectly for texts. Please confirm the time after we book, just in case!
Agent: Perfect, we’ll use this number for the text confirmation.  

Quickly, what’s your last name, Sofia?
User: Rodriguez! And I run the brokerage in Houston, remember? Also, confirming tomorrow. What time again?
Agent: Right, Sofia Rodriguez with the brokerage in Houston — got you.  

One quick thing before I offer times: which time zone are you in there — Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: Oh, right! I'm in the Mountain... wait, no, Central Time Zone. Yep, Central!
Agent: Nice, Central it is — same as us, so that makes it easy.  

For tomorrow, I can get you in at either 11:30 am or 12:15 pm Central for that 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay — which one fits better with your day?
User: 12:15 pm works! Please reconfirm this time later. Can't wait to fix this call chaos.
Agent: Nice, 12:15 pm Central tomorrow it is.  

Quick thing — what’s the best number to reach you on?
User: Oh, of course! Reach me at (713) 555-1234. Please confirm the time again later!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that for you.
Agent: Perfect, Sofia — you’re all set for tomorrow at 12:15 pm Central with Jay. You’ll get an SMS confirmation at this number in a moment, and from that text you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if anything changes.

Is there anything else I can help you with before I let you go?

Alright, really glad you called in today — this is going to make a big dent in that call chaos. Have a great rest of your day, and we’ll talk tomorrow. Bye!
